fear_greed.commentary: Fear & Greed is stuck at 17, extreme fear, essentially unchanged from Monday's close even after the rebound; it is down from 30 a week ago and about level with a month ago.

markets.summary: Stocks gave back part of Monday's Nvidia-fueled surge: the S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,201.09 and the Nasdaq slid 1.48% to 23,733.54, while the Dow gained 0.85% to 50,018.70. Tech led the decline as Nvidia dropped 5.9% to $155.38 and an index of semiconductors fell 7.9%, with investors also bracing for possible new tariffs. All three indexes remain below their 40-week averages with RSI around 40. Small caps held up better, with the Russell 2000 up 0.57% to 2,684.94, and the 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.90%. Gold futures fell 2.45% to about $3,562 and silver futures 5.5% to about $40.76, both still well under their 40-week averages ahead of Wednesday's PCE inflation data. Breadth improved slightly to 55.2% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average, still neutral, while Fear & Greed remains in extreme fear.

weather.summary: A strong coastal storm forming off the Southeast on Wednesday will ride up the East Coast through Thanksgiving, bringing 1-4 inches of rain to the Mid-Atlantic, gusts over 50 mph at the coast and significant coastal flooding from the Outer Banks to New Jersey. Wintry precipitation may reach the Mid-Mississippi Valley Thursday into Friday, while rain and high-elevation snow continue in the Pacific Northwest.
